cards.explanation: The answer is that Christ Jesus will judge the living and the dead. Paul says Christ Jesus "…will judge the living and the dead…" (2 Timothy 4:1). He says it right as he gives Timothy a charge, so this is serious business, friends. Paul also mentions Christ's appearing and His kingdom in the same breath. That's the kind of sentence you read standing up.

The answer is True. Paul's list is "reprove, rebuke, and encourage…" (2 Timothy 4:2). Encouragement sits right there next to the tough stuff. I think that's a good reminder, bakers, that correcting and cheering somebody on can come from the same teacher.

The answer is patient. Paul says "…every form of patient instruction." (2 Timothy 4:2). Reproving, rebuking and encouraging all get done with patience. I think patience is easy to say and hard to do, friends, especially when I'm waiting on a batch and the oven is taking its sweet time.

The answer is that they gather teachers to suit their own desires. Paul says "…with itching ears they will gather around themselves teachers to suit their own desires." (2 Timothy 4:3). They don't stop listening. They just pick the teachers who say what they already want to hear. That's like asking for a recipe and only accepting the one that says cookies for dinner, forever.

The answer is myths. Paul says they "…will turn their ears away from the truth and turn aside to myths." (2 Timothy 4:4). Truth walks out and myths walk in. I'd call that a rough trade, friends, like swapping a fresh batch for a picture of cookies.

The answer is False. Paul tells Timothy to "endure hardship" (2 Timothy 4:5), not steer clear of it. The same verse says to be sober in all things, do the work of an evangelist and fulfill his ministry. Hardship is part of the road, friends, and Timothy is told to keep walking.

The answer is fulfill. Paul says "…fulfill your ministry." (2 Timothy 4:5). He wants Timothy to see it through. It's like a batch that goes all the way from dough to box instead of getting abandoned on the counter.

The answer is that he stayed faithful all the way to the end. Paul says "I have fought the good fight, I have finished the race, I have kept the faith." (2 Timothy 4:7). Three lines, and they all say he stayed with it. Notice, bakers, he doesn't brag about being perfect. He says he kept going and kept the faith.

The answer is False. Paul says the Lord will award the crown "…not only to me, but to all who crave His appearing." (2 Timothy 4:8). He includes others in the promise. I'd say that's a pretty generous thing to say, friends.

The answer is True. Paul says the crown of righteousness is something "…the Lord, the righteous Judge, will award to me on that day…" (2 Timothy 4:8). He says it's laid up for him. It's a prize he's looking forward to, friends, and he says who hands it out.

The answer is appearing. Paul says "…all who crave His appearing." (2 Timothy 4:8). The crown is for those who long for the Lord to appear. That's also why my ovens stay ready, friends. I don't know the day, but I keep them warm.
